title: Bauhaus
content: Apply Bauhaus design principles with form follows function philosophy. Use primary colors (red, blue, yellow) plus black and white. Geometric shapes: circles, squares, triangles as core elements. Clean sans-serif typography (Futura, DIN, Helvetica). Grid-based asymmetric layouts. Bold contrast between elements. Minimal decoration - every element serves purpose. Include iconic Bauhaus color blocking. Strong horizontal and vertical lines. Industrial, functional aesthetic.

variants.simple: Create functional modernist design inspired by Bauhaus school with primary colors and geometric forms.
variants.detailed: Apply Bauhaus design principles with form follows function philosophy. Use primary colors (red, blue, yellow) plus black and white. variants.advanced: Apply Bauhaus design principles (1919-1933 German modernist school). Color theory: primary colors as accents (red-600 #E53935, blue-600 #1E88E5, yellow-500 #FDD835) against black and white base. Geometric foundation: circle, square, triangle as core visual vocabulary - use consistently for icons, decorations, layouts. Typography: geometric sans-serif (Futura, DIN, Bauhaus 93, ITC Avant Garde), clean letterforms, strong hierarchy through size and weight. Layout: asymmetric grid compositions, dynamic balance, intentional white space. Form follows function: every element has purpose, no pure decoration. Color blocking: large areas of solid color creating visual rhythm. Lines: bold horizontal and vertical rules as structural elements, thin lines for division. Shapes as containers: content within geometric frames. Josef Albers color squares: nested squares demonstrating color interaction. Material honesty: design suggests industrial production, machine-made precision. Interactive: geometric transitions, shapes morphing on state changes. Modern implementation: CSS Grid for Bauhaus-style compositions, custom properties for color palette. Accessibility: high contrast from limited palette, clear functional hierarchy aids navigation. Educational context: perfect for design schools, architecture, modern art contexts.
